description: Equipment designation naming convention for electrical SLD systems. Defines the structured format for panel/equipment tags used across the SLD pipeline. Part of the data layer. It adds NEC-517 essential-electrical-system coverage that the segment grammar previously could not express (closing the 32 TI-4 designation gaps recorded in 02_specs/drafting/sld_topology_rules_V1_0_0.md §7). Additions: power_type codes C (Critical Branch) and EQ (Equipment Branch); equipment codes MSB (Main Switchboard), G (Generator), FP (Fire Pump); and a new top-level special_designations section for tags that fall outside the [PowerType][Voltage][Equipment]-[Level]-[Identifier] grammar (an exact-match allowlist and a documented FUT future/spare infix rule), consumed data-driven by validator TI-4. All additions are real NEC-517 / distribution concepts (source: hospital narrative branches), not fabrications. The additive level_code_labels / level_code_pattern keys (per A-7 WI-5(b)) are carried forward UNCHANGED — the renderer engine mirrors only those two keys. The value tables remain a faithful mirror of the source xlsx (no R row added; the level table is declared extensible). Owner addition 2026-10-20: equipment code K (Kitchen Panel), added to this JSON and to the source xlsx together.

power_type.description: Power source classification. Blank = Normal Power. Codes LS, C and EQ are the NEC 517 essential electrical system branches (Life Safety / Critical / Equipment) used on hospital SLDs, completing the three-branch set on the A-7 designation card.

values.notes: Default when no prefix is present

NEC 517 essential electrical system — life safety branch (illumination of means of egress, exit signs, alarm/alerting, emergency communication, generator-set loads per NEC 517.32). Two-character code; TI-4 matches longest-code-first, so LS is distinguished from L (Legally Required Power).
NEC 517 essential electrical system — critical branch (life-safety-adjacent patient-care loads). Covers hospital C… designations.
NEC 517 essential electrical system — equipment branch (delayed-automatic-connection equipment loads). Covers hospital EQ… designations.

voltage.description: System voltage tier encoded as single-digit or two-digit code.

equipment.description: Equipment type abbreviation. Codes MSB, G and FP cover main-switchboard, generator and fire-pump equipment present on the golden cases.

values.notes: Owner addition 2026-10-20 (Clinic AI Test, 2K-1-A = 208V kitchen panel, Level 1, instance A). Single-letter code; no other equipment code is K or starts with K, so the longest-code-first TI-4 match is unaffected.
Service-entrance / main switchboard. Covers office 4MSB… / E4MSB… designations (legend previously had MDP only).
Generator equipment when tagged inside the segment grammar (e.g. E4G…). The two-segment generator source tag GEN-1 is handled by special_designations.exact_match.
Fire-pump controller / feed (e.g. E4FP…). Covers the hospital fire-pump designation.

special_designations.description: Valid as-built designations that do NOT fit the [PowerType][Voltage][Equipment] – [Level] – [Identifier] segment grammar. Consumed data-driven by validator TI-4 (08_validation/rules/ti_rules_V1_0_0.mjs) so that acceptance of these tags is declared here in the data layer, not hardcoded in the rule. Separator normalization (spaced en-dash ≡ compact hyphen) is applied by the consumer before matching. Source: hospital narrative branches.

exact_match.description: Generator, first in series
exact_match.notes: NEC 517 essential electrical system source. Two-segment tag (equipment abbreviation + sequential number); the generator source is drawn without a Power Type/Voltage prefix and without a Level segment, so it cannot be expressed by the segment grammar. Additional in-series generators (GEN-2, …) would be added here as exact matches.

infix_rules.name: Future / Spare
infix_rules.description: Reserved-for-future (spare) equipment. FUT appears as an INFIX between the Equipment segment and the Level segment: [PowerType][Voltage][Equipment]-FUT-[Level]-[Identifier]. The base tag otherwise follows the normal segment grammar.
infix_rules.notes: Marks a provisioned-but-unequipped position (a spare tap left for future build-out). Covers the office 4S-FUT… designation. Consumers permit the infix optionally between equipment and level; because no level code equals an infix code, the extension only adds acceptance for FUT-tagged spares and changes no other tag's parse.

level.description: Building level / floor. Extensible beyond listed values.

identifier.description: Sequential alphabetic identifier for multiple instances of the same equipment type at the same level. Extensible.
